title: Opening of Paradise Lost
text: Of Man's first disobedience, and the fruit / Of that forbidden tree whose mortal taste / Brought death into the World, and all our woe, / With loss of Eden, till one greater Man / Restore us, and regain the blissful seat.
translation_en: Of Man's first disobedience, and the fruit of that forbidden tree whose mortal taste brought death into the World, and all our woe, with loss of Eden, till one greater Man restore us, and regain the blissful seat.

title: Opening of A Tale of Two Cities
text: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness, it was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity.
translation_en: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness, it was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity.
source: Charles Dickens, A Tale of Two Cities

title: English Proverb Collection
text: A stitch in time saves nine. The early bird catches the worm. Actions speak louder than words. All that glitters is not gold. Better late than never.
translation_en: A stitch in time saves nine. The early bird catches the worm. Actions speak louder than words. All that glitters is not gold. Better late than never.

title: Opening of Don Quixote
text: En un lugar de la Mancha, de cuyo nombre no quiero acordarme, no ha mucho tiempo que vivía un hidalgo de los de lanza en astillero, adarga antigua, rocín flaco y galgo corredor.
translation_en: In a village of La Mancha, the name of which I have no desire to call to mind, there lived not long since one of those gentlemen that keep a lance in the lance-rack, an old buckler, a lean hack, and a greyhound for coursing.

title: Neruda - Poema 20
text: Puedo escribir los versos más tristes esta noche. Escribir, por ejemplo: La noche está estrellada, y tiritan, azules, los astros, a lo lejos.
translation_en: I can write the saddest verses tonight. Write, for example: The night is starry, and the blue stars shiver in the distance.
source: Pablo Neruda, Veinte poemas de amor

title: Spanish Proverbs
text: No hay mal que por bien no venga. Más vale tarde que nunca. Dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres. El que mucho abarca poco aprieta.
translation_en: Every cloud has a silver lining. Better late than never. Tell me who you walk with and I'll tell you who you are. He who grasps much holds little.

title: Opening of The Stranger
text: Aujourd'hui, maman est morte. Ou peut-être hier, je ne sais pas. J'ai reçu un télégramme de l'asile: «Mère décédée. Enterrement demain. Sentiments distingués.» Cela ne veut rien dire.
translation_en: Today, mother died. Or maybe yesterday, I don't know. I received a telegram from the home: "Mother deceased. Funeral tomorrow. Faithfully yours." That doesn't mean anything.

title: Baudelaire - L'Albatros
text: Souvent, pour s'amuser, les hommes d'équipage / Prennent des albatros, vastes oiseaux des mers, / Qui suivent, indolents compagnons de voyage, / Le navire glissant sur les gouffres amers.
translation_en: Often, to amuse themselves, the men of a crew catch albatrosses, vast sea birds, that follow, indolent companions of the voyage, the ship gliding over the bitter depths.
source: Charles Baudelaire, Les Fleurs du mal

title: French Proverbs
text: L'habit ne fait pas le moine. Petit à petit, l'oiseau fait son nid. Qui vivra verra. Il ne faut pas vendre la peau de l'ours avant de l'avoir tué.
translation_en: The habit does not make the monk. Little by little, the bird builds its nest. Who lives will see. Don't sell the bear's skin before you've killed it.

title: Opening of The Metamorphosis
text: Als Gregor Samsa eines Morgens aus unruhigen Träumen erwachte, fand er sich in seinem Bett zu einem ungeheueren Ungeziefer verwandelt.
translation_en: When Gregor Samsa awoke one morning from troubled dreams, he found himself transformed in his bed into a monstrous vermin.

title: Goethe - Erlkönig
text: Wer reitet so spät durch Nacht und Wind? Es ist der Vater mit seinem Kind; er hat den Knaben wohl in dem Arm, er fasst ihn sicher, er hält ihn warm.
translation_en: Who rides so late through night and wind? It is the father with his child; he holds the boy well in his arm, he clasps him securely, he keeps him warm.

title: German Proverbs
text: Übung macht den Meister. Morgenstund hat Gold im Mund. Wer zuletzt lacht, lacht am besten. Aller Anfang ist schwer.
translation_en: Practice makes perfect. The morning hour has gold in its mouth. He who laughs last, laughs best. Every beginning is hard.

title: Opening of The Divine Comedy
text: Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita / mi ritrovai per una selva oscura, / ché la diritta via era smarrita.
translation_en: In the middle of the journey of our life, I found myself within a dark forest, for the straight way was lost.

title: Opening of The Name of the Rose
text: Naturalmente, un manoscritto. Il 16 agosto 1968 mi fu messo fra le mani un libro dovuto alla penna di tale abate Vallet.
translation_en: Naturally, a manuscript. On August 16, 1968, I was handed a book written by a certain Abbot Vallet.
source: Umberto Eco, Il nome della rosa

title: Italian Proverbs
text: Chi dorme non piglia pesci. Tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare. A caval donato non si guarda in bocca. Ogni lasciata è persa.
translation_en: He who sleeps catches no fish. Between saying and doing lies the sea. Don't look a gift horse in the mouth. Every opportunity left is lost.

title: Opening of The Lusiads
text: As armas e os Barões assinalados / Que da Ocidental praia Lusitana / Por mares nunca de antes navegados / Passaram ainda além da Taprobana.
translation_en: The arms and the heroes renowned, who from the Western Lusitanian shore, through seas never sailed before, passed even beyond Taprobana.

title: Opening of The Posthumous Memoirs of Brás Cubas
text: Algum tempo hesitei se devia abrir estas memórias pelo princípio ou pelo fim, isto é, se poria em primeiro lugar o meu nascimento ou a minha morte.
translation_en: For some time I hesitated whether to open these memoirs at the beginning or at the end, that is, whether to put my birth or my death first.
source: Machado de Assis, Memórias Póstumas de Brás Cubas

title: Portuguese Proverbs
text: Água mole em pedra dura, tanto bate até que fura. Quem não tem cão, caça com gato. De grão em grão, a galinha enche o papo.
translation_en: Soft water on hard stone, strikes until it bores through. He who has no dog, hunts with a cat. Grain by grain, the hen fills her crop.

title: Opening of Anna Karenina
text: Все счастливые семьи похожи друг на друга, каждая несчастливая семья несчастлива по-своему.
transliteration: Vse schastlivye sem'i pokhozhi drug na druga, kazhdaya neschastlivaya sem'ya neschastliva po-svoyemu.
translation_en: All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.

title: Pushkin - I Loved You
text: Я вас любил: любовь ещё, быть может, / В душе моей угасла не совсем; / Но пусть она вас больше не тревожит; / Я не хочу печалить вас ничем.
transliteration: Ya vas lyubil: lyubov' yeshchyo, byt' mozhet, / V dushe moyey ugasla ne sovsem; / No pust' ona vas bol'she ne trevozhit; / Ya ne khochu pechalit' vas nichem.
translation_en: I loved you: love yet, perhaps, in my soul has not quite died away; but let it trouble you no longer; I do not wish to sadden you in any way.

title: Russian Proverbs
text: Тише едешь — дальше будешь. Без труда не выловишь и рыбку из пруда. Век живи — век учись.
transliteration: Tishe yedesh' — dal'she budesh'. Bez truda ne vylovish' i rybku iz pruda. Vek zhivi — vek uchis'.
translation_en: The quieter you go, the further you'll get. Without labor you won't pull a fish from a pond. Live a century — learn a century.

title: Opening of the Quran - Al-Fatiha
text: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ ﴿١﴾ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ﴿٢﴾ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ ﴿٣﴾ مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ ﴿٤﴾
transliteration: Bismi-llāhi r-raḥmāni r-raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu li-llāhi rabbi l-ʿālamīn. Ar-raḥmāni r-raḥīm. Māliki yawmi d-dīn.
translation_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to God, Lord of all the worlds. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Master of the Day of Judgment.

title: The Mu'allaqat - Imru' al-Qais
text: قِفا نَبكِ مِن ذِكرى حَبيبٍ وَمَنزِلِ / بِسِقطِ اللِّوى بَينَ الدَّخولِ فَحَومَلِ
transliteration: Qifā nabki min dhikrā ḥabībin wa-manzili / bi-siqṭi l-liwā bayna d-dakhūli fa-ḥawmali
translation_en: Stop, let us weep at the remembrance of a beloved and a dwelling place / at the edge of the sand dune between al-Dakhūl and Ḥawmal.

title: Arabic Proverbs
text: اللي ما يعرف الصقر يشويه. الصبر مفتاح الفرج. من جدّ وجد ومن زرع حصد.
transliteration: Illi mā yaʿrif aṣ-ṣaqr yishwīh. Aṣ-ṣabr miftāḥ al-faraj. Man jadda wajada wa-man zaraʿa ḥaṣad.
translation_en: He who doesn't know the falcon grills it. Patience is the key to relief. He who strives finds, and he who sows reaps.

title: Opening of"Dream of the Red Chamber
text: 满纸荒唐言，一把辛酸泪。都云作者痴，谁解其中味？
transliteration: Mǎn zhǐ huāngtáng yán, yī bǎ xīnsuān lèi. Dōu yún zuòzhě chī, shuí jiě qí zhōng wèi?
translation_en: Full of absurd words on every page, a handful of bitter tears. All say the author is mad, who can understand its flavor?
source: Cao Xueqin, Dream of the Red Chamber

title: Opening of"A Madman's Diary
text: 今天晚上，很好的月光。我不見他，已是三十多年；今天見了，精神分外爽快。
transliteration: Jīntiān wǎnshang, hěn hǎo de yuèguāng. Wǒ bù jiàn tā, yǐ shì sānshí duō nián; jīntiān jiàn le, jīngshén fènwài shuǎngkuài.
translation_en: Tonight, very good moonlight. I haven't seen him for over thirty years; today when I saw him, my spirits felt especially refreshed.

title: Chinese Proverbs
text: 学而不思则罔，思而不学则殆。三人行必有我师焉。千里之行始于足下。
transliteration: Xué ér bù sī zé wǎng, sī ér bù xué zé dài. Sān rén xíng bì yǒu wǒ shī yān. Qiān lǐ zhī xíng shǐ yú zú xià.
translation_en: To study without thinking is futile; to think without studying is dangerous. Among three people walking, there must be one who can teach me. A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.

title: Opening of Godan
text: होरी ने दोनों बैलों को, जो पहले से द्वार पर खड़े पागुर कर रहे थे, गाड़ी में जोता और एक घड़ा पानी लेकर खेत की ओर चला।
transliteration: Horī ne donõ bailõ ko, jo pahle se dvār par khaṛe pāgur kar rahe the, gāṛī mẽ jotā aur ek ghaṛā pānī lekar khet kī or calā.
translation_en: Hori yoked both bullocks, which had been standing at the door chewing cud, to the cart, and carrying a pitcher of water, headed toward the field.

title: Kabir Doha
text: बुरा जो देखन मैं चला, बुरा न मिलिया कोय। जो मन खोजा आपना, मुझसे बुरा न कोय।
transliteration: Burā jo dekhan main calā, burā na miliyā koy. Jo man khojā āpnā, mujhse burā na koy.
translation_en: When I went out looking for evil, I found none. When I searched my own mind, I found none worse than myself.

title: Hindi Proverbs
text: जैसा देश वैसा भेष। जहाँ चाह वहाँ राह। बंदर क्या जाने अदरक का स्वाद।
transliteration: Jaisā deś vaisā bheṣ. Jahā̃ cāh vahā̃ rāh. Bandar kyā jāne adrak kā svād.
translation_en: When in Rome, do as the Romans do. Where there is a will, there is a way. What does a monkey know of the taste of ginger?

title: Opening of The Tale of Genji
text: いづれの御時にか、女御、更衣あまたさぶらひたまひけるなかに、いとやむごとなき際にはあらぬが、すぐれて時めきたまふありけり。
transliteration: Izure no ohon-toki ni ka, nyōgo, kōi amata saburaitamaikeru naka ni, ito yamgotonaki kiwa ni wa aranu ga, sugurete tokimekitamau arikeri.
translation_en: In a certain reign there was a lady not of the first rank whom the emperor loved more than any of the others.
source: Murasaki Shikibu, The Tale of Genji

title: Matsuo Bashō - Haiku
text: 古池や蛙飛び込む水の音。閑さや岩にしみ入る蝉の声。夏草や兵どもが夢の跡。
transliteration: Furuike ya / kawazu tobikomu / mizu no oto. Shizukasa ya / iwa ni shimiiru / semi no koe. Natsukusa ya / tsuwamono-domo ga / yume no ato.
translation_en: An old pond — a frog jumps in, sound of water. Silence — seeping into the rocks, the cicada's cry. Summer grass — where warriors once dreamed.

title: Japanese Proverbs
text: 七転び八起き。猿も木から落ちる。石の上にも三年。出る杭は打たれる。
transliteration: Nana korobi ya oki. Saru mo ki kara ochiru. Ishi no ue ni mo san nen. Deru kui wa utareru.
translation_en: Fall seven times, stand up eight. Even monkeys fall from trees. Three years on a stone (patience). The nail that sticks out gets hammered down.

title: Opening of The Vegetarian
text: 아내가 채식주의자가 되기 전까지만 해도, 나는 그녀가 특별한 사람이라고 생각한 적이 없었다.
transliteration: Anaega chaesikjuuijaga doegi jeonkkajiman haedo, naneun geunyeoga teukbyeolhan sarami-rago saenggakhan jeogi eopseotda.
translation_en: Before my wife turned vegetarian, I had always thought of her as completely unremarkable in every way.

title: Yun Dong-ju - Counting the Stars
text: 죽는 날까지 하늘을 우러러 한 점 부끄러움이 없기를, 잎새에 이는 바람에도 나는 괴로워했다.
transliteration: Jungneun nalkkaji haneureul ureoreo han jeom bukkeureoumeul eopgireul, ipsaee ineun baramedo naneun goerowohaetda.
translation_en: Until the day I die, let me gaze up at the sky with not a speck of shame. Even the wind in the leaves tormented me.
source: Yun Dong-ju, Counting the Stars at Night

title: Korean Proverbs
text: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다. 콩 심은 데 콩 나고, 팥 심은 데 팥 난다. 세 살 버릇 여든까지 간다.
transliteration: Nanmareun saega deutgo bammareun jwiga deunneunda. Kong simeun de kong nago, pat simeun de pat nanda. Se sal beoreut yeodeunkkaji ganda.
translation_en: Birds hear the words spoken in the day, mice hear the words spoken at night. Plant beans and you get beans, plant red beans and you get red beans. Habits formed at three last until eighty.

title: Opening of My Name is Red
text: Şimdi ben bir ölüyüm, bir ceset, bir kuyunun dibinde. Son nefesimi çoktan verdim, kalbim durdu.
translation_en: I am nothing but a corpse now, a body at the bottom of a well. I took my last breath ages ago, my heart stopped.
source: Orhan Pamuk, My Name Is Red

title: Nazim Hikmet - On Living
text: Yaşamak şakaya gelmez, büyük bir ciddiyetle yaşayacaksın, bir sincap gibi mesela, yani, yaşamanın dışında ve ötesinde hiçbir şey beklemeden.
translation_en: Living is no laughing matter: you must live with great seriousness, like a squirrel, for example — I mean without looking for something beyond and above living.

title: Turkish Proverbs
text: Damlaya damlaya göl olur. Bir elin nesi var, iki elin sesi var. Sakla samanı gelir zamanı. Aç tavuk kendini buğday ambarında sanır.
translation_en: Drop by drop, a lake forms. One hand has nothing, two hands have a voice. Save the straw, its time will come. A hungry chicken dreams it's in a wheat barn.

title: Swahili Proverb Collection
text: Haraka haraka haina baraka. Asiyefunzwa na mamaye hufunzwa na ulimwengu. Penye nia pana njia. Kidole kimoja hakivunji chawa.
translation_en: Hurry hurry has no blessing. He who is not taught by his mother is taught by the world. Where there is a will, there is a way. A single finger cannot crush a louse.

title: Shaaban Robert - Poem
text: Titi la mama litamu, lijapoacha na utamu. Lisilo na mama lina, mwana hulia machozi.
translation_en: The breast of one's mother is sweet; even when it dries, the sweetness remains. Without a mother, the child cries tears.

title: Opening of Siku Njema
text: Siku hiyo nilikuwa nimefurahi sana. Siku hiyo ilikuwa siku njema kwangu, siku ambayo sitaisahau kamwe.
translation_en: That day I was very happy. That day was a good day for me, a day that I will never forget.

title: Cavafy - Ithaca
text: Σα βγεις στον πηγαιμό για την Ιθάκη, / να εύχεσαι νάναι μακρύς ο δρόμος, / γεμάτος περιπέτειες, γεμάτος γνώσεις.
transliteration: Sa vgeis ston pigaimó gia tin Itháki, na éfchesai nánai makrýs o drómos, gemátos peripéteies, gemátos gnóseis.
translation_en: As you set out for Ithaca, hope the voyage is a long one, full of adventure, full of discovery.

title: Opening of Zorba the Greek
text: Πρώτη φορά τον είδα στον Πειραιά. Είχα κατεβεί στο λιμάνι ν'αποχαιρετίσω μιαν φίλη που ταξίδευε για τη Κρήτη.
transliteration: Próti forá ton eída ston Peiraiá. Eícha kateveí sto limáni n'apochairetíso mian fíli pou taxídeve gia ti Kríti.
translation_en: I first met him at Piraeus. I had gone down to the port to say goodbye to a friend who was traveling to Crete.

title: Greek Proverbs
text: Σιγά σιγά και το αυγό μαδάει. Όποιος βιάζεται σκοντάφτει. Τα πολλά λόγια είναι φτώχεια.
transliteration: Sigá sigá kai to avgó madáei. Ópoios viázetai skontáftei. Ta pollá lógia eínai ftócheia.
translation_en: Slowly, slowly, even the egg loses its feathers. He who hurries stumbles. Too many words are poverty.

title: Opening of the Aeneid
text: Arma virumque cano, Troiae qui primus ab oris / Italiam, fato profugus, Laviniaque venit / litora, multum ille et terris iactatus et alto.
translation_en: I sing of arms and the man, who first from the shores of Troy, exiled by fate, came to Italy and the Lavinian shores — much buffeted on land and on the deep.

title: Opening of the Vulgate Bible - Genesis
text: In principio creavit Deus caelum et terram. Terra autem erat inanis et vacua, et tenebrae erant super faciem abyssi, et spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas.
translation_en: In the beginning God created heaven and earth. And the earth was without form, and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God moved upon the waters.

title: Opening of the Iliad
text: Μῆνιν ἄειδε, θεά, Πηληϊάδεω Ἀχιλῆος / οὐλομένην, ἣ μυρί' Ἀχαιοῖς ἄλγε' ἔθηκε.
transliteration: Mēnin áeide, theá, Pēlēïádeō Achilēos / ouloménēn, hḕ murí' Achaioĩs álge' éthēke.
translation_en: Sing, O goddess, the anger of Achilles, son of Peleus, that brought countless ills upon the Achaeans.

title: Opening of the Rigveda
text: अग्निमीळे पुरोहितं यज्ञस्य देवमृत्विजम् । होतारं रत्नधातमम् ॥
transliteration: Agnim īḷe purohitaṃ yajñasya devam ṛtvijam. Hotāraṃ ratnadhātamam.
translation_en: I praise Agni, the chosen priest, god, minister of sacrifice, the hotar, lavisher of wealth.

title: Opening of Beowulf
text: Hwæt! We Gardena in geardagum, / þeodcyninga, þrym gefrunon, / hu ða æþelingas ellen fremedon.
translation_en: Lo! We have heard of the glory of the Spear-Danes, of the kings of the people, in the days of old, how the princes performed courageous deeds.

title: Hávamál - Words of the High One
text: Deyr fé, deyja frændr, deyr sjalfr it sama; en orðstírr deyr aldregi hveim er sér góðan getr.
translation_en: Cattle die, kinsmen die, you yourself die likewise; but the fame of the one who has earned good repute will never die.

title: Lord's Prayer in Gothic
text: Atta unsar þu in himinam, weihnai namo þein. Qimai þiudinassus þeins. Wairþai wilja þeins, swe in himina jah ana airþai.
translation_en: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

title: Hymn to Inanna
text: nin me šár-ra an ki-a diğir zi u₃-tud-da nú-me-a
translation_en: Lady of all the divine powers, resplendent light, righteous woman clothed in radiance, beloved of Heaven and Earth.

title: Code of Hammurabi - Prologue
text: inūma Anum ṣīrum šar Anunnakī Enlil bēl šamê u erṣetim šā'im šīmat māt nišī Mardukim māršu rēštiam ša Ea ellūtam ina teništim ušarši'ūšum
translation_en: When the august god Anu, king of the Anunnaki, and the god Enlil, lord of heaven and earth, who determines the destinies of the land, allotted supreme power over all peoples to Marduk.

title: Pangur Bán
text: Messe ocus Pangur Bán, cechtar nathar fria shaindán: bíth a menma-sam fri seilgg, mu menma céin im shaíncheirdd.
translation_en: Me and Pangur Bán, each of us at his special art: his mind is set on hunting, my mind on my special craft.

title: Opening of the Dao De Jing
text: 道可道，非常道。名可名，非常名。無名天地之始。有名萬物之母。
transliteration: Dào kě dào, fēi cháng dào. Míng kě míng, fēi cháng míng. Wú míng tiāndì zhī shǐ. Yǒu míng wànwù zhī mǔ.
translation_en: The Dao that can be told is not the eternal Dao. The name that can be named is not the eternal name. The nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth. The named is the mother of the ten thousand things.

title: Opening of Max Havelaar
text: Ik ben makelaar in koffie, en woon op de Lauriergracht No 37. Het is mijn gewoonte niet, romans te schrijven, of zulke dingen.
translation_en: I am a coffee broker, and I live at No. 37 Lauriergracht. It is not my custom to write novels or such things.

title: Vondel - Gijsbrecht van Aemstel
text: Het hemelsche gerecht heeft zich ten langen leste erbarremt over het schreien en kerme der stadt.
translation_en: The heavenly court has at long last taken pity on the crying and lamenting of the city.
source: Joost van den Vondel, Gijsbrecht van Aemstel

title: Dutch Proverbs
text: Wie een kuil graaft voor een ander, valt er zelf in. Oost west, thuis best. De appel valt niet ver van de boom.
translation_en: He who digs a pit for another falls in it himself. East west, home is best. The apple doesn't fall far from the tree.

title: Opening of Pippi Longstocking
text: I utkanten av en liten, liten stad lag en gammal forfallen tradgard, och i tradgarden lag ett gammalt hus, och i huset bodde Pippi Langstrump.
translation_en: On the outskirts of a tiny little town lay an old overgrown garden, and in the garden stood an old house, and in the house lived Pippi Longstocking.

title: Tegner - Frithiofs Saga
text: Sol skiner over Hildings sal, och blommorna dofta derinom; men Frithiof sitter tyst i skuggan och Ingeborg sitter vid hans sida.
translation_en: The sun shines over Hilding's hall, and flowers fragrance within; but Frithiof sits quietly in the shadow, and Ingeborg sits by his side.

title: Swedish Proverbs
text: Battre sent an aldrig. Den som gapar efter mycket mister ofta hela stycket. Ovning ger fardighet.
translation_en: Better late than never. He who gapes after much often loses the whole piece. Practice makes perfect.

title: Opening of Hunger
text: Det var i den tid jeg gikk omkring og sultet i Kristiania, denne forunderlige by som ingen forlater for han har fatt merker av den.
translation_en: It was in those days when I wandered about hungry in Kristiania, that strange city which no one leaves before it has set its mark upon him.

title: Norwegian Proverbs
text: Ingen roser uten torner. Ovelse gjor mester. Borte bra, men hjemme best.
translation_en: No roses without thorns. Practice makes perfect. Away is good, but home is best.

title: Opening of Out of Africa
text: Jeg havde en farm i Afrika ved foden af Ngong-bjergene.
translation_en: I had a farm in Africa, at the foot of the Ngong Hills.

title: Danish Proverbs
text: Ovelse gor mester. Man skal ikke saelge skindet, for bjornen er skudt. Mange baekke sma gor en stor a.
translation_en: Practice makes perfect. Don't sell the skin before the bear is shot. Many small streams make a big river.

title: Opening of Pan Tadeusz
text: Litwo! Ojczyzno moja! ty jestes jak zdrowie; Ile cie trzeba cenic, ten tylko sie dowie, Kto cie stracil.
translation_en: Lithuania! My fatherland! You are like health; how much you should be valued, only he who has lost you can know.

title: Opening of Quo Vadis
text: Petroniusz obudzil sie zaledwie kolo poludnia i jak zwykle byl mocno znuzony.
translation_en: Petronius woke barely around noon and as usual was greatly fatigued.

title: Polish Proverbs
text: Kto rano wstaje, temu Pan Bog daje. Nie ma rozy bez kolcow. Co sie odwlecze, to nie uciecze.
translation_en: He who rises early, God provides for. There is no rose without thorns. What is postponed does not escape.

title: Opening of The Good Soldier Svejk
text: Tak nam zabili Ferdinanda, rekla posluhovacka panu Svejkovi, ktery opustil pred lety vojenskou sluzbu.
translation_en: So they've killed our Ferdinand, said the charwoman to Mr. Svejk, who had left military service years before.
source: Jaroslav Hasek, Osudy dobreho vojaka Svejka

title: Czech Proverbs
text: Bez prace nejsou kolace. Kdo jinemu jamu kopa, sam do ni pada. Rano moudrejsi vecera.
translation_en: Without work there are no cakes. He who digs a pit for another falls into it himself. The morning is wiser than the evening.

title: Eminescu - Luceafarul
text: A fost odata ca-n povesti, a fost ca niciodata. Din rude mari imparatesti, o prea frumoasa fata.
translation_en: Once upon a time, as never before, from great imperial lineage, a most beautiful maiden.

title: Romanian Proverbs
text: Cine sapa groapa altuia cade singur in ea. Ce tie nu-ti place altuia nu-i face.
translation_en: He who digs a pit for another falls in it himself. Do not do unto others what you would not have done to you.

title: Petofi - Nemzeti dal
text: Talpra magyar, hi a haza! Itt az ido, most vagy soha! Rabok legyunk vagy szabadok? Ez a kerdes, valasszatok!
translation_en: Rise up, Hungarians, the homeland calls! Here is the time, now or never! Shall we be slaves or free? That is the question, choose!

title: Hungarian Proverbs
text: Gyakorlat teszi a mestert. Lassan jarj, tovabb ersz. Ki koran kel, aranyat lel.
translation_en: Practice makes the master. Go slowly, you'll get further. He who rises early finds gold.

title: Opening of the Kalevala
text: Mieleni minun tekevi, aivoni ajattelevi, lahteani laulamahan, saa'ani sanelemahan.
translation_en: I am driven by my longing, and my understanding urges, that I should commence my singing, and begin my recitation.

title: Finnish Proverbs
text: Ei kukaan ole seppa syntyessaan. Hiljaa hyva tulee. Ken kuuseen kurkottaa, se katajaan kapsahtaa.
translation_en: No one is born a blacksmith. Good things come slowly. He who reaches for the spruce falls into the juniper.

title: Opening of Truth and Justice
text: Andres oli viie-aastane poiss, kui ta isa Pearu talust viimaks ara tuli ja oma kohta Vargamaele asus.
translation_en: Andres was a five-year-old boy when his father finally left Pearu's farm and settled in his own place at Vargamae.
source: A. H. Tammsaare, Tode ja oigus

title: Estonian Proverbs
text: Harjutamine teeb meistriks. Kes teisele auku kaevab, see ise sisse kukub. Hommik on ohtust targem.
translation_en: Practice makes a master. He who digs a pit for another falls in himself. The morning is wiser than the evening.

title: Opening of The Knight in the Panther's Skin
text: რომელმან შექმნა სამყარო ძალითა მით ძლიერითა, ზეცით ბოძებულ ქვეყანას მისგან მართ ხორციერითა.
transliteration: Romelm-an shek'mna samq'aro dzalita mit dzlierita, zetsit botsebul kveq'anas misgan mart k'ortsiierita.
translation_en: He who created the universe by His mighty power, bestowed upon the world from heaven through His corporeal.
source: Shota Rustaveli, The Knight in the Panther's Skin

title: Georgian Proverbs
text: ბრძენი მტერი სჯობია უგუნურ მეგობარს. მოთმინება ვარდს მოიტანს.
transliteration: Brdzeni mteri sjobia ugunur megobars. Motmineba vards moitans.
translation_en: A wise enemy is better than a foolish friend. Patience brings roses.

title: Charents - I Love My Sweet Armenia
text: Es im anush Hayastani arevahot varder vayr, es sirumem khort khosen dardzer hnatsen sev laler.
transliteration: Es im anush Hayastani arevahot varder vayr, es sirumem khort khosen dardzer hnatsen sev laler.
translation_en: I love my sweet Armenia's sun-baked words, I love the ancient, dark laments.
source: Yeghishe Charents, I Love My Sweet Armenia

title: Armenian Proverbs
text: Arants k'ami dzar ch'i sharzhvum. Kanukh astgh-y vaghch' ch'i mtnum. Lav e ushan k'an verj.
transliteration: Arants k'ami dzar ch'i sharzhvum. Kanukh astgh-y vaghch' ch'i mtnum. Lav e ushan k'an verj.
translation_en: A tree doesn't move without wind. An early bird doesn't go hungry. Better late than never.

title: Opening of In the City of Slaughter
text: קום לך לך אל עיר ההריגה ובאת אל החצרות
transliteration: Kum lekh lekh el ir ha-hariga u-vata el ha-chatserot.
translation_en: Arise and go to the city of slaughter, and you shall come to the courtyards.
source: Chaim Nachman Bialik, In the City of Slaughter

title: Hebrew Proverbs
text: אל תסתכל בקנקן אלא במה שיש בו. הכל צפוי והרשות נתונה.
transliteration: Al tistakel be-kankan ela be-ma she-yesh bo. Ha-kol tsafui ve-ha-reshut netuna.
translation_en: Do not look at the vessel but at what is in it. Everything is foreseen, yet freedom of choice is given.

title: Hafez - Ghazal
text: اگر آن ترک شیرازی به دست آرد دل ما را / به خال هندویش بخشم سمرقند و بخارا را
transliteration: Agar an Tork-e Shirazi be-dast arad del-e ma ra, be khal-e Hendu-yash bakhsham Samarqand o Bokhara ra.
translation_en: If that Shirazi Turk takes my heart in hand, for her Hindu mole I'd give Samarkand and Bukhara.

title: Persian Proverbs
text: دیر آید درست آید. هر که بامش بیش برفش بیشتر. یک دست صدا ندارد.
transliteration: Dir ayad dorost ayad. Har ke bamash bish barfash bishtar. Yek dast seda nadarad.
translation_en: What comes late comes right. He whose roof is higher has more snow. One hand makes no sound.

title: Tagore - Gitanjali Opening
text: আমার মাথা নত করে দাও হে তোমার চরণধুলার তলে। সকল অহংকার হে আমার ডুবাও চোখের জলে।
transliteration: Amar matha nat kore dao he tomar charandular tale. Sakal ahankar he amar dubao chokher jale.
translation_en: Bow down my head in the dust at your feet, O Lord. Drown all my pride in my tears.

title: Bengali Proverbs
text: অতি চালাকের গলায় দড়ি। যত গর্জে তত বর্ষে না। নাচতে না জানলে উঠোন বাঁকা।
transliteration: Ati chalaker golay dori. Jato gorje tato borshe na. Nachte na janle uthon banka.
translation_en: The rope is around the neck of the over-clever. It doesn't rain as much as it thunders. A bad dancer blames the stage.

title: Thirukkural - Opening
text: அகர முதல எழுத்தெல்லாம் ஆதி பகவன் முதற்றே உலகு.
transliteration: Akara mudala ezhuththellaam aadhi bhagavan mudhatre ulagu.
translation_en: As all letters have 'A' as their first, so the world has the eternal God as its first.

title: Tamil Proverbs
text: ஆத்திரக்காரனுக்கு புத்தி மட்டு. விழுந்தாலும் மூக்குடைபடாமல் விழணும்.
transliteration: Aathirakkaaranukku puththi mattu. Vizhundhaalum mukkudaipadaamal vizhanum.
translation_en: An angry person has limited wisdom. Even if you fall, fall without breaking your nose.

title: Vemana - Verse
text: ఉప్పు కప్పురంబు నొక్కపోలికనుండు, చూడ చూడ రుచుల జాడ తెలియు.
transliteration: Uppu kappurambu nokkapolikanuṇḍu, chuuda chuuda ruchula jaada teliyu.
translation_en: Salt and camphor look alike, but only upon tasting does the difference become clear.

title: Telugu Proverbs
text: అడిగేవాడికి చెప్పేవాడు లోకువ. చేతులు కాలాక ఆకులు పట్టుకోవడం.
transliteration: Adigevaadiki cheppevaadu lokuva. Chetulu kalaaka aakulu pattukkovaḍaṃ.
translation_en: The teller is less important than the asker. Grabbing leaves after the hands are burned.

title: Opening of The Judgement
text: เมื่อฟ้าสางแดดแรกโผล่ขึ้นมา ชีวิตก็เริ่มตื่นขึ้นอีกครั้ง
transliteration: Muea faa saang daet raek phlo khuen ma, chiwit ko roem tuen khuen ik khrang.
translation_en: When dawn breaks and the first sunlight appears, life awakens once again.

title: Thai Proverbs
text: น้ำขึ้นให้รีบตัก. ช้าๆได้พร้าเล่มงาม. รู้จักเขา รู้จักเรา รบร้อยครั้ง ชนะร้อยครั้ง.
transliteration: Nam khuen hai rip tak. Cha cha dai phra lem ngam. Ru chak khao ru chak rao rop roi khrang chana roi khrang.
translation_en: When the water rises, hurry to scoop it. Slowly, slowly you get a fine axe. Know your enemy, know yourself, fight a hundred battles win a hundred.

title: Opening of The Tale of Kieu
text: Tram nam trong coi nguoi ta, chu tai chu menh kheo la ghet nhau.
translation_en: In this world of a hundred years, talent and fate have always been at odds.

title: Vietnamese Proverbs
text: Co cong mai sat co ngay nen kim. Uong nuoc nho nguon. An qua nho ke trong cay.
translation_en: With enough grinding, iron becomes a needle. When drinking water, remember its source. When eating fruit, remember who planted the tree.

title: Burmese Buddhist Text
text: သိပ္ပံပညာသည် အတတ်ပညာ၏ အရင်းအမြစ်ဖြစ်သည်။
transliteration: Thipan pyinnya thi atatpyinnya ei ayinmyit phyit thi.
translation_en: Scientific knowledge is the foundation of all learning.

title: Burmese Proverbs
transliteration: Kywe ku ye nwa pa ku. Sa tat kyi len sa chwut kyi.
translation_en: When the buffalo crosses the river, the cow follows. The great scholar also makes great mistakes.

title: Reamker - Opening
text: រាមកេរ្តិ៍ ជាសាច់រឿងរបស់ព្រះរាម ដែលជារឿងរ៉ាវពីប្រាសាទអង្គរ។
transliteration: Reamker chea sach roeung robos preah Ream del chea roeung rav pi prasat Angkor.
translation_en: The Reamker is the story of Lord Rama, a tale from Angkor temple.

title: Khmer Proverbs
text: ឆ្កែកំព្រា ស្តេចមិនខ្វល់។ ទឹកឡើង ត្រីស៊ីស្រមោច ទឹកហោច ស្រមោចស៊ីត្រី។
transliteration: Chkae komprea sdech min khvol. Tuk laeng trei si sramaoch tuk haoch sramaoch si trei.
translation_en: The king doesn't care about a stray dog. When water rises, fish eat ants; when water recedes, ants eat fish.

title: Opening of This Earth of Mankind
text: Namaku Minke, satu nama yang masih selalu asing di telingaku sendiri. Seorang pribumi dengan nama Eropa.
translation_en: My name is Minke, a name still always strange to my own ears. A native with a European name.

title: Indonesian Proverbs
text: Air tenang menghanyutkan. Berakit-rakit ke hulu, berenang-renang ke tepian. Sedikit demi sedikit, lama-lama menjadi bukit.
translation_en: Still waters run deep. Raft upstream, swim to the shore. Little by little, over time it becomes a hill.

title: Rizal - Noli Me Tangere Opening
text: Noong isang gabi ng buwan ng Oktubre, si Don Santiago de los Santos, na kilala sa tawag na Kapitan Tiyago, ay nag-aanyaya ng isang hapunan.
translation_en: One evening in the month of October, Don Santiago de los Santos, commonly known as Captain Tiago, was giving a dinner party.

title: Tagalog Proverbs
text: Ang hindi marunong lumingon sa pinanggalingan ay hindi makakarating sa paroroonan. Kung may tinanim, may aanihin.
translation_en: He who does not look back to where he came from will not reach his destination. If you plant, you shall harvest.

title: Yoruba Oriki - Praise Poetry
text: Ogun laa fi idi ire si. Ise loogba omo aruuwa. Ohun ti a ba fi owo otun gbin, owo osi a fi mu.
translation_en: War is how we establish good fortune. Work is the friend of the fortunate. What the right hand plants, the left hand harvests.

title: Yoruba Proverbs
text: Bi a ba n la odo aja, a fi odo eniyan si. Agba ki wa loja ki ori omo titun wo. Ika to ba gun eni, eni na lo nmu.
translation_en: When we cross the dog's river, we include the human's river. An elder does not stay in the market while a child's head goes crooked. The finger that hurts you is the one you bite.

title: Zulu Praise Song - Shaka
text: UNodumehlezi kaMenzi, uShaka wasehlathini ubeyinkosi. Igazi elimhlophe belingasakhi.
translation_en: Nodumehlezi son of Menzi, Shaka of the forest was a king. The white blood could no longer build.

title: Zulu Proverbs
text: Inkomo ingazala inkunzi. Umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu. Inyoni yakhela ngoboya benye.
translation_en: A cow can give birth to a bull. A person is a person through other people. A bird builds its nest with other birds' feathers.

title: Ethiopian Kebra Nagast
text: ይህ ታሪክ ስለ ንግሥተ ሳባ እና ስለ ንጉሥ ሰሎሞን መገናኘት ነው።
transliteration: Yih tarik sile nigiste Saba inna sile nigus Selomon megegnagnet new.
translation_en: This is the story of the Queen of Sheba and her meeting with King Solomon.

title: Amharic Proverbs
text: ሰው በሰው ይመካል። ዘገየ ቢመጣ ሞት ቢቀድም ያድናል። የወደቀ ቢነሳ ያልተሳሳተ ይመስላል።
transliteration: Sew be-sew yimekal. Zgeye bimet'a mot bik'edim yadinal. Yewedek'e binesa yaltesasate yimeslal.
translation_en: A person relies on people. Better late than never — it saves from death. He who falls and rises seems like he never stumbled.

title: Hausa Oral Tradition
text: Labari na da can, wani sarki yana da yara bakwai. Yara sun girma sun zama jarumawa masu karfi.
translation_en: A story from long ago, a certain king had seven children. The children grew up to become brave warriors of great strength.

title: Hausa Proverbs
text: Gaskiya ta fi kwabo. Aiki ba karfe ba ne. Kowa ya dafa dahuwa ya ci dahuwa.
translation_en: Truth is worth more than a penny. Work is not iron. Whoever cooks a porcupine must eat porcupine.

title: Inca Prayer to Viracocha
text: Wiraqucha, Pachakamaq, Tiqsi Wiraqucha, qammi kay pachata rurarqanki, runakunata kamarqanki.
translation_en: Viracocha, Creator of the World, Foundation Viracocha, you made this world, you formed humanity.

title: Quechua Proverbs
text: Ama suwa, ama llulla, ama qilla. Huk umalla, huk makilla, huk sunqulla.
translation_en: Do not steal, do not lie, do not be lazy. One mind, one hand, one heart.

title: Nahuatl Flower Song
text: Xochitl in cuicatl ye nican on yoliya noyollo ipalnemohuani. In tepetl in atl in ixtlahuatl ye nican.
translation_en: Flower and song here my heart lives, O Giver of Life. The mountain, the water, the plain are here.

title: Nahuatl Proverbs
text: In tlahtolli ihuan in nehnemiliztli zan ce. Nelli ye nican tontlapihuia in tlalticpac.
translation_en: Word and deed are one. Truly here on earth we are but borrowed.

title: Hawaiian Creation Chant - Kumulipo
text: O ke au i kahuli wela ka honua. O ke au i kahuli lole ka lani. O ke au i kukaiaka ka la.
translation_en: When the earth became hot. When the heavens turned about. When the sun was darkened.

title: Hawaiian Proverbs
text: I ka olelo no ke ola, i ka olelo no ka make. Aia no ka pua i luna, ke onaona mai la i ka ihu.
translation_en: In language there is life, in language there is death. When the flower is above, the fragrance reaches the nose.

title: Maori Haka - Ka Mate
text: Ka mate, ka mate! Ka ora! Ka ora! Tenei te tangata puhuruhuru nana nei i tiki mai whakawhiti te ra.
translation_en: I die! I die! I live! I live! This is the hairy man who caused the sun to shine again.

title: Maori Proverbs
text: He aha te mea nui o te ao. He tangata, he tangata, he tangata. Ehara taku toa i te toa takitahi.
translation_en: What is the greatest thing in the world? It is people, it is people, it is people. My strength is not that of a single warrior.

title: Opening of Milarepa's Songs
text: བླ་མ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་ལ་ཕྱག་འཚལ་ལོ། སྐྱབས་སུ་མཆི་བ་ཡིན།
transliteration: Lama rinpoche la chak tshallo. Kyab su chi wa yin.
translation_en: I bow to the precious teacher. I take refuge.

title: Tibetan Proverbs
text: ལམ་རིང་པོ་བགྲོད་མཁན་ཁ་ཤས་ནི་ལམ་ཐུང་བར་ཕྱིན་ཡོད།
transliteration: Lam ringpo drod khan kha she ni lam thungwar chin yod.
translation_en: Some who set out on a long road arrived on a short one.

title: Opening of The Secret History of the Mongols
text: Чингис хааны өвөг дээдэс нь дээд тэнгэрээс заяатай төрсөн бөртэ чоно ажээ.
transliteration: Chingis khaany ovog deedes ni deed tengerrees zayaatai torson borte chono ajee.
translation_en: The ancestor of Chinggis Khan was a blue-gray wolf born by the will of Heaven above.
source: The Secret History of the Mongols

title: Mongolian Proverbs
text: Нэг хүний зовлон нийт хүмүүсийн зовлон. Сурсан мэдсэнээс сурах зүйл их.
transliteration: Neg khunii zovlon niit khumuusiin zovlon. Sursan medsenees surakh zuil ikh.
translation_en: One person's suffering is everyone's suffering. There is more to learn than what has been learned.

title: Bertsolaritza - Oral Poetry
text: Munduan zehar ibilli naiz herri askotara joan naiz, baina nere herria da nere bihotzean beti daukadana.
translation_en: I have traveled the world, I have gone to many lands, but my homeland is what I always carry in my heart.

title: Basque Proverbs
text: Etxean ondo bizi dena ez da hemendik joango. Hitz gutxi eta lan asko. Gaizki hasia ondoan bukatzen da.
translation_en: He who lives well at home will not leave. Few words and much work. What starts badly ends soon.

title: Behistun Inscription of Darius
text: adam Darayavaus xsayathiya vazraka xsayathiya xsayathiyanam xsayathiya Parsaiy.
translation_en: I am Darius, the Great King, King of Kings, King in Persia.

title: Gospel of Thomas - Opening
text: Nai ne mmaje ethep ejau ais etont auw afsjau nau nje didymos ioudas thomas.
translation_en: These are the secret words which the living Jesus spoke, and which Didymus Judas Thomas wrote down.

title: Hittite Treaty Preamble
text: Um-ma dUTU-si mMur-si-li LUGAL.GAL LUGAL KUR URUHa-at-ti UR.SAG.
translation_en: Thus says My Sun, Mursili, the Great King, King of the Land of Hatti, the Hero.

title: Ahuna Vairya Prayer
text: Yatha ahu vairyo atha ratush ashat chit hacha, vangheush dazda manangho shyaothananam angheush mazdai.
translation_en: As the Master, so the Judge to be chosen in accord with truth. The gifts of good mind are for the deeds done in this world for Mazda.

title: Opening of the Gospel of John
text: Iskoni be slovo i slovo be ou boga i bogb be slovo.
translation_en: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
source: Old Church Slavonic Bible, Gospel of John

title: Opening of the Book of the Dead
text: Djed medu in Wsir Ani maakheru, hena Netjeru aaut em Duat.
translation_en: Words spoken by the Osiris Ani, justified, with the great gods in the underworld.
source: Book of the Dead, Papyrus of Ani

title: Inscription of King Hiram of Byblos
text: arn z pala yitmilk mlk gbl bn ahibal mlk gbl lyitmilk mlk gbl.
translation_en: This coffin was made by Ittobaal, king of Byblos, son of Ahibaal, king of Byblos, for Ittobaal king of Byblos.

title: Tocharian Love Poem Fragment
text: Sana masa somo klainatstse yaitka postana se nesau.
translation_en: Now then, through woman's wiles, afterwards I was not.

title: Aramaic Prayer from Daniel
text: Elaha di-shemaya malkhuta yehav lakh, hayla viqara vetushbakhta.
translation_en: The God of heaven has given you dominion, power, glory, and praise.

title: Hildebrandslied
text: Ik gihorta dat seggen, dat sih urhettun aenon muotin, Hiltibrant enti Hadubrant, untar heriun tuem.
translation_en: I heard tell that two warriors, Hildebrand and Hadubrand, met in single combat between two armies.

title: Mem and Zin - Opening
text: Di nav cihan da bav u kal, hemiya xorteki bi nav u mal.
translation_en: In this world, fathers and elders, there was once a young man of fame and fortune.

title: Kurdish Proverbs
text: Dost di roja resin da diyar dibe. Yek bi yek dibe du. Kesib kese, dewlemend kerkese.
translation_en: A friend is known on a rainy day. One by one makes two. The poor are sparrows, the rich are vultures.

title: Ibsen - A Doll's House
text: En herlig ting er det med livet, Torvald: det er jo aldeles fullt av vidunderlige hemmeligheter.
translation_en: A wonderful thing about life, Torvald: it is absolutely full of wonderful secrets.

title: Kierkegaard - Either/Or
text: Hvad er en Digter? Et ulykkeligt Menneske, der gjemmer dybe Kvaler i sit Hjerte.
translation_en: What is a poet? An unhappy person who conceals deep sorrows in his heart.

title: Capek - R.U.R.
text: Helena, jsem Alquist, stavitel Rossumovych Univerzalnich Robotu.
translation_en: Helena, I am Alquist, builder of Rossum's Universal Robots.

title: Opening of Ion
text: Inceputul a fost la jocul din Pripas. Satul era asezat pe coastele blajine ale dealurilor.
translation_en: The beginning was at the dance in Pripas. The village was settled on the gentle slopes of the hills.

title: Moricz - Be Faithful Unto Death
text: A nyolceves gyerek felrezte almabol a korai harangszot.
translation_en: The eight-year-old child was awakened from his dreams by the early bell.

title: Kivi - Seven Brothers Opening
text: Jukolassa, Toukolan vanhalla talolla, asui seitseman veljesta, jotka isan kuoltua ryhtyivat taloa hoitamaan.
translation_en: In Jukola, the old Toukola estate, lived seven brothers who, after their father's death, took over running the farm.

title: Tammsaare - Truth and Justice
text: Pearu ajas ennast istukilt pusti ja vaatas uhkelt ule Vargamae lagendiku.
translation_en: Pearu rose from his seat and looked proudly over the Vargamae lowlands.
source: A. H. Tammsaare, Tode ja oigus

title: Indonesian National Pledge
text: Kami putra dan putri Indonesia, mengaku bertumpah darah yang satu, tanah air Indonesia.
translation_en: We the sons and daughters of Indonesia, acknowledge one homeland, the land of Indonesia.

title: Tagalog Love Poetry - Florante at Laura
text: Kapwa nagtiis ng dalita't hirap, sa mundong ibabaw kaparis ng dilim.
translation_en: Both suffered grief and hardship, in the world above, companions of darkness.

title: Hausa Story Opening
text: A zamanin da, wani babban birni yana da wani sarki mai adalci da hikima.
translation_en: In times past, a great city had a king of justice and wisdom.

title: Vazha-Pshavela - The Snake Eater
text: მთაში ერთი კაცი ცხოვრობდა, რომელსაც გველის ჭამა სჩვეოდა.
transliteration: Mtashi erti k'atsi tskhovrobda, romelsats gvelis ch'ama sch'veoda.
translation_en: In the mountains lived a man who had a habit of eating snakes.
